transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Head of ML - LatticeCare), Tomio Reyes (CTO), Priya Nair (PM), Ben Ortiz (DevOps), Aisha Khan (Data Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Short session to align on POC success criteria and model candidates. Agreed to run a 4-week POC: week 1 baseline runs, week 2 refine prompts and config, week 3 stress/latency tests, week 4 consolidation + handoff.

[00:00:07] Maya Chen: hi everyone uh thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Elena here, hi
[00:00:14] Tomio Reyes: Tomio here
[00:00:16] Priya Nair: Priya
[00:00:18] Ben Ortiz: Ben -- hello
[00:00:21] Maya Chen: great, Samir from infra is on -- Samir can you intro what we'll run through?
[00:00:27] Samir Patel: yeah hi all, SE at Redwood. We'll cover scope, what "good" looks like for you, workloads, then propose a model shortlist and bench plan. Also quick note on VPC and security options.

[00:00:45] Priya Nair: to ground things, our use case is clinical note extraction - structured fields for diagnosis, med lists, and also short summary generation. We need Spanish and Portuguese support as well, about 20% of docs non-EN.
[00:00:57] Dr. Elena Ruiz: and important, all data must be de-id'd but we want the benchmark to run on realistic clinical snippets, including HL7 fragments.

[00:01:10] Samir Patel: ok, thanks. Quick qualification: expected steady QPS for inference?
[00:01:16] Ben Ortiz: baseline will be low initially. Maybe 5-10 QPS for the POC, but bursty up to ~50 qps during batch ingest.
[00:01:25] Tomio Reyes: timeline: we want to decide on vendor and approach by end of May. so a 4-week POC in April/May fits.

[00:01:38] Maya Chen: perfect. let's talk success criteria — what would make this a win for you?
[00:01:43] Priya Nair: accuracy: entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our validation set; summary ROUGE-L above our current baseline which is 0.42. Also P95 latency for single-turn inference under 250ms for 128 token calls.
[00:01:57] Dr. Elena Ruiz: and privacy — logs must be auditable, and we need KMS integration for key wrapping. SOC2 plus HIPAA readiness info will be required.

[00:02:12] Samir Patel: noted — we have a SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration options; we'll send those links. For latency targets, small models with q4 quantization often hit low p95; larger models give quality but cost more.

[00:02:33] [00:02:33] Ben Ortiz: question on private deployment — can we do VPC peering for the test runner or do we need an on-prem appliance?
[00:02:40] Samir Patel: we can run the benchmark in a Redwood private env with VPC peering and temporary peered workspace; for strict air gap we'd need the private on-prem bundle which adds setup time. For POC, VPC peering is usually fine.

[00:02:59] Maya Chen: model shortlist we recommend for this workload (open models):
[00:03:04] Samir Patel: 1) Llama-2-13B (q4_0) - strong generalist, good for instruction and extraction with prompt engineering;
[00:03:11] Samir Patel: 2) Mosaic MPT-7B-instruct (q4) - cheaper, lower latency, slightly lower extraction accuracy in early tests;
[00:03:18] Samir Patel: 3) XGen-multi-8B (multilingual) - trained for multilingual intent, good for ES/PT, mid-range latency;
[00:03:25] Samir Patel: 4) Falcon-40B-mini? (note: heh - sometimes transcription says falcon forty but we actually meant Falcon-7B or Falcon-40b-v2 depending on infra) - FLAG: heavier but high quality on generative tasks;
[00:03:40] Samir Patel: 5) Mosaic-ML MPT-30B-lite (if we need better quality) -- though cost and latency increase.

[00:03:48] Dr. Elena Ruiz: are these available quantized to 4-bit? we need to understand tradeoffs.
[00:03:52] Samir Patel: yes q4 options for many; q4_0, q4_k, and some 3-bit/4-bit experimental paths. Important caveat: 4-bit can affect extraction tokenization edge cases. We'll include the delta experiments in bench runs.

[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Priya Nair: for multilingual: XGen looks promising but how does Llama-2-13B fare on Spanish and Portuguese?
[00:04:17] Samir Patel: Llama 13B is okay with prompt translation but XGen-multi typically outperforms on ES/PT classification/extraction out of box. We propose testing both and measuring entity F1 by language slice.

[00:04:32] Maya Chen: let's walk through the benchmark plan — Samir?
[00:04:36] Samir Patel: plan outline:
- Week 1 (baseline): run the same inference runner against each candidate model on 1k anonymized notes provided by the customer. Measure p95/p99 latency, throughput, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, extraction F1 by language slice.
- Week 2 (config): prompt tuning, caching, prefix KV cache experiments and batching tweaks; try q4 vs q8 quant configs.
- Week 3 (stress): concurrency up to target bursts (50 QPS), long-context tests (1k tokens), and stability runs; check memory/KV eviction patterns.
- Week 4 (handoff): consolidate results, recommendations, run a short runbook with DevOps for integration and initial SLA estimate.

[00:05:12] Tomio Reyes: what metrics will you capture for cost? just model cost or infra too?
[00:05:16] Samir Patel: both. We'll produce per-token cost estimates (compute + infra) and effective cost per successful extraction. We'll also show expected monthly costs at steady state and at 50 qps burst.

[00:05:30] [00:05:30] Ben Ortiz: about the runner — will it run inside our VPC or use Redwood infra?
[00:05:36] Samir Patel: for the POC we'll offer two options: 1) runbench inside a Redwood private workspace with VPC peering (recommended), or 2) provide a dockerized runner to run in your environment. Option 1 gets quicker metrics; option 2 gives you full control.

[00:05:52] Aisha Khan: we'll likely pick VPC peering for speed, but need instructions for IAM/peering.
[00:05:57] Maya Chen: we'll send the runbook. Also note logging: we can mask logs and provide audit-only traces per token id; full text logs can be disabled.

[00:06:08] Priya Nair: what about evaluation for extraction — what's the harness? exact span match or relaxed?
[00:06:13] Samir Patel: we can run both: strict exact span F1 and a normalized entity match that tolerates small offsets. We'll include confusion matrices and per-entity precision/recall.

[00:06:26] Dr. Elena Ruiz: for acceptance, the F1 should be measured on held-out set — not the training examples. we'll provide a held-out 2k set for final validation.

[00:06:34] Maya Chen: great. Any quick concerns on private deployment?
[00:06:38] Ben Ortiz: one is key management. We use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys; will Redwood support bringing your own KMS?
[00:06:46] Samir Patel: yes BYOK via KMS integrations; we'll include HSM details in the security doc.

[00:06:55] [00:06:55] Priya Nair: timeline again — can you run Week 1 baseline by 2026-04-16 if we deliver samples by 2026-04-12?
[00:07:02] Maya Chen: we'll aim for that. Samir, is that doable?
[00:07:05] Samir Patel: yes, assuming samples are uploaded and anonymized. We'll spin up the private bench and send initial results by 2026-04-16 EOD.

[00:07:16] Tomio Reyes: on model selection — we prefer smaller models if they meet F1 — cost matters. What's your recommendation cutoff?
[00:07:23] Samir Patel: pragmatic rule: if a 7B model gets within 3-4% absolute F1 of the 13B for extraction, we recommend the 7B for production because of better latency/cost; else 13B or 30B variants if you need higher generative quality.

[00:07:35] Maya Chen: let's surface one more point — caching and prefix reuse. If the majority of notes contain repeated templates, token-based caching gives big wins.
[00:07:44] Aisha Khan: yes we have templated discharge summaries — that's a good fit for prefix caching.

[00:07:50] [00:07:50] Ben Ortiz: any blockers on HIPAA / BAAs for POC?
[00:07:54] Maya Chen: Redwood can sign a BAA; for POC we'll still anonymize data but BAA paperwork is standard. I'll attach the security packet.

[00:08:04] Priya Nair: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps?
[00:08:08] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood sends benchmark runner + security docs (links) by 2026-04-09. 2) LatticeCare uploads anonymized 1k sample by 2026-04-12. 3) Redwood runs baseline and shares results by 2026-04-16. 4) Follow-up meeting 2026-04-23 to review and decide expansion.

[00:08:30] Tomio Reyes: thanks everyone.
[00:08:33] Dr. Elena Ruiz: thanks
[00:08:35] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

[00:08:50] End of recording

Notes on transcription artifacts: some model names and quant flags were auto-transcribed oddly (e.g., "q four" vs "q4_k"). Also a couple interruptions; timestamps approximate.
